warnings: Show a gentle notice if supplements alone average more than 100 µg (4,000 IU) per day over 7 days and are not marked as prescribed.
Spread weekly doses: 60,000 IU (1,500 µg) once a week averages about 214 µg/day, above the UL; usually a short doctor-supervised course.
Flag stacking when two or more vitamin D-containing products are logged on the same day.
Prompt for a doctor review if a weekly 60,000 IU course runs beyond 8 weeks without a prescribed flag.
Never warn on food or sunlight; sun exposure cannot cause vitamin D toxicity.
IFCT 2017 plant vitamin D2 values are low confidence and are excluded from the progress ring by default.
People with kidney disease, kidney stones, sarcoidosis, high calcium, or on thiazide diuretics or digoxin should seek medical advice before supplementing.
Upper limit 100 µg (4,000 IU) a day from food plus supplements (NASEM, EFSA); ICMR TUL not found
60,000 IU sachets and 600,000 IU injections are doctor-set treatment courses, not daily supplements; taking the weekly dose daily has caused toxicity in India
Count every product: calcium-D3, multivitamin and D3 drops add up
IFCT 2017 plant vitamin D values (ragi, curry leaves, soya, mushrooms) are implausible and must not be shown
Fortified milk and oil amounts conflict between sources: use the pack label
Sunlight is not counted as intake; avoid sunburn
General information, not medical advice; pregnancy, kidney disease, stones and regular medicines need a doctor
